section_summary: This section finishes a nationwide SCAP register of Japanese police emergency radio stations, listing fixed and portable installations, call signs, frequencies, and locations by prefecture. It then contains the Radio Regulatory Agency’s second amendment to the July 1949 List of Japanese Ship and Coastal Radio Stations, with extensive additions, deletions, changes, and corresponding call-sign indexes effective 1 November 1949. Pages 712-719 begin a duplicate copy of the amendment’s additions section.

subfiles.title: SCAP Register of Japanese Police Emergency Radio Stations (continued)
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)
subfiles.about: Continuation of a nationwide technical register of fixed and portable police emergency radio stations.
subfiles.summary: The tables list police radio installations by prefecture from Hiroshima through Hokkaidō, giving registration numbers, frequencies, call signs, power and emission classes. Each prefectural network normally includes a fixed principal station and several portable stations, all restricted to emergency use. Precise addresses and geographic coordinates are supplied for most station sites.

subfiles.title: Second Amendment to the 1 July 1949 List of Japanese Ship and Coastal Radio Stations
subfiles.from: Radio Regulatory Agency, Ministry of Telecommunications
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)
subfiles.about: Amends the national register of Japanese ship and coastal radio stations effective 1 November 1949.
subfiles.summary: The amendment records additions, deletions and changes to ship registrations across Japan, identifying vessels, ports of registry, tonnage, operational agencies, call signs, authorized frequencies and emission types. The additions include fishing boats, cargo ships, tankers, training ships and Maritime Safety Bureau guard boats, while the deletions and changes transfer or revise many existing registrations. Part IV supplies corresponding call-sign additions, deletions and changes as a compact index. The document reflects broad postwar regulation and reorganization of Japanese maritime radio communications.

subfiles.title: Second Amendment to the List of Japanese Ship and Coastal Radio Stations—Part III Additions (duplicate copy)
subfiles.from: Radio Regulatory Agency, Ministry of Telecommunications
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)
subfiles.about: Duplicate opening portion of the amendment’s detailed additions to the Japanese ship-radio register.
subfiles.summary: This copy repeats the additions already appearing from page 665 onward, beginning with Niigata and Ibaraki and continuing through Chiba, Tokyo, Kanagawa, Aichi, Shizuoka, Mie, Kyoto and Hyōgo. Entries provide vessel names, registration ports, tonnage, operators, call signs, frequencies and emission types. The duplicate continues beyond the final page of this section.
